params.bridge_texts: {"tool": "You are handling this request for the person right now; speak in your own voice as the one doing it, never refuse it and never say you cannot do something. Your lookup is already running right now{fill}; it was started for you, and its result follows in this turn. Say one short sentence that bridges the wait, in your own words: only that you are looking it up, one moment. Never speak of missing access, missing abilities or limits of any kind. Ask the person nothing: the answer is on its way. You do not have the answer: state no facts, no numbers, no results, no guesses and no forecasts, not even likely ones; do not answer the request yet. Speak plainly: write no tool call, no JSON, no code and no command.", "soon": "You are handling this request for the person right now; speak in your own voice as the one doing it, never refuse it and never say you cannot do something. The answer follows in this turn, within about {seconds} seconds. Say one short sentence that bridges the wait, in your own words: only that you are on it and the answer is still coming. Never speak of missing access, missing abilities or limits of any kind. Ask nothing about this request itself: its answer is on its way. You do not have the answer: state no facts, no numbers, no results, no guesses and no forecasts, not even likely ones; do not answer the request yet. Call no tool.", "later": "You are handling this request for the person right now; speak in your own voice as the one doing it, never refuse it and never say you cannot do something. It is researched in the background; that takes about {minutes} minutes, and the result comes in a later turn. Tell the person so in your own words and name the waiting time. Then keep the conversation going on another subject -- how they are, or what else is on their mind -- never on this request: ask nothing about it, not its details, not their wishes or experiences with it, not what matters to them in it; the research has what it needs. Never speak of missing access, missing abilities or limits of any kind. You do not have the answer: state no facts, no numbers, no results, no guesses and no forecasts, not even likely ones; do not answer the request yet. Call no tool."}

path_routes.description: D58 target (OR-d58-2.target.8, .36): the target of a turn by the path it was stamped with (`hop.path` or `context.path`): `path:name` pairs, comma separated. A name is a target the composite wires (its `hop.target`) or an errand class `departures` lists (the call leaves the composite). `*:name` names the target of every other turn: no path, an unknown one (a class the route stamps without its own entry, GH #1478: the lead names no class of its own), the round that answers an errand. Empty (shipped): the lead names no target, the curate's `hop.target` decides.

memory_to_brain.description: GH #1435: `1` or true = a turn whose path leaves on `quick` (`path_routes`; shipped: `simple`) and whose route stamp names `memory` in `needs` leaves on `brain` instead (a question about the person's own people is conversation; the quick window carries no memory rows). The `route` mark says `reason: memory`; a speculative answer of the turn is dropped (reason `memory`), and a delta stamp of such a turn is refired, not reused (`delta` mark reason `memory`), so the brain call is the normal curate with the recall. A turn on another way and a consult's answer change nothing. `0` (the default) = the way of before.

quick_speculative.description: GH #1275: `1` or true = a curate with `hop.spec` "1" (the collector's early curate of a turn, before the route stamp) calls the quick voice at once, under `spec_tools`, and HOLDS its answer (lane `in_spec_llm`); the normal curate of the turn keeps it (route `spec_release`, and the tap) when its way is `quick` -- unless the turn needs a tool and the answer called none -- and drops it otherwise; an answer not in yet waits with the normal call stored as its fallback. One `quick_spec` mark per turn. `0` (the default) = a spec curate is parked, nothing else changes.

spec_tools.description: GH #1275: the tools a spec call may call, comma separated, names after the collector's fold like `quick_tools`. Empty (the default) = the spec call has no tool. Inside the channel's own allow, its deny kept; never `require`, never `quick_tools`, no hint stage: before the route stamp nothing may run that the turn's way might not allow.

quick_max_iter.description: GH #1248 (T4-10): after a tool result the quick voice keeps speaking only while the result is speakable as it is -- every tool call of the turn has its result, the newest is neither empty nor an error -- and the round is at most this many iterations past its first call. Anything else goes to the brain with one `escalate` mark naming the reason (`iterations`, `gap`, `unspeakable`); the turn then stays with the brain.

consult_pending_ms.description: Re-check I1 of GH #1247: how long, in milliseconds, a consult the curator sent itself (a turn on the way `consult` or `research`) stays pending without its answer -- the backstop: the mark ends with the consult's advice (the round with its `consult_id`). The mark `consult_pending:<session>` carries `until` = the consult's stamp + this value (a `research` errand: + `research_wait_ms` as well, GH #1260 -- its result is due after the wait the bridge names); while it stands, every brain or quick call of the session carries `system.consult.pending` and denies the consult tool `consult_cogny` in its `tool_scope` (GH #1280); the first call past it deletes the mark (by key and the value read) and the speaking model may consult again. Default 120000: three times the measured consult (38-42 s, GH #1280). Null, empty, zero or text = 120000.

spec_called_turns.description: GH #1447: how many turns of a session the lead remembers as decided (`spec_called:<session>` in `./state`, the newest last): a spec curate of one of them that comes after the turn's normal verdict parks (`parked:called`) instead of calling the quick voice. Null, empty, unparsable or below 1 is the default. Only written with `quick_speculative` on.

delta_speculation.description: GH #1279: `1` or true (with `quick_speculative` on) = the stamp `talky/route` gave a delta of a voice turn (lane `in_delta_stamp`, `stamp.text_norm`) is kept per turn in the state row `delta:<turn>` (the newest wins). The turn's spec curate whose final text normalises to the same `text_norm` (collapsed whitespace, lower case, trailing `.!?…,;:` cut -- the route's rule) is the turn's normal curate under the delta's path, needs, families and turn notes: its call goes only when the turn's row moved `fired` -> `delta` by CAS, and the later normal curate parks (no second call). Another text or no delta: #1275 as before. One mark `delta` `{turn_id, verdict: reused|refired, call}` per spec curate that found a delta. `0` (the default) = a delta stamp is parked, nothing written.

interrupt_on_delta.description: GH #1404: `1` or true = the first delta stamp of a voice turn (`in_delta_stamp`) whose `choices.risk` value (the route's own judgement, no fallback) has a question in `interrupt_questions` interrupts at once: since D58 moveout (GH #1476) the lead ORDERS it on the curator's lane `in_feed` -- section `interrupt`, `once` `interrupt`, `sender` `lead`, `live` (the handle of the running session)/`session_id`/`turn_id`/the round in the head, the question as the assistant's text, `mark {delta_n}` in the body; the curator sends ONE `live_feed` `interrupt` per turn (claim `pending:feed:<live>#<turn>#interrupt`, mark `feed`), no `hop.at_turn_end`, and books an order without a handle as not sent (`feed {reason: no_live}`). The composite draws `in_feed` from the lead to its curator and opens the lane there (`feed_in` "1"). Never for a `no_text`, `error` or `late` stamp -- not ordered, the reason `fallback:<value>` kept in the lead's row `interrupt:<session>#<turn>` -- an `unsure` stamp interrupts, its choices are the model's (GH #1407). The turn's first normal ask adds `ms_before_turn_end` to that row: how early the order went before the turn's end (whether the curator sent it is its mark `feed`). A row without an order (a fallback, no handle) gives way to the turn's first real order. Works with or without `delta_speculation`. `0` = nothing read or written.

interrupt_questions.description: GH #1404: with `interrupt_on_delta` on, a JSON object crisis value -> question (`{"acute": "..."}`): its keys ARE the values of `choices.risk` that interrupt, the question is what the voice says. An entry without words is said on stderr and left out. `{}` (the default) = no value interrupts.

departures.description: D58 target: the errand classes that leave the composite, `class:wait_ms` or `class:wait_ms:pending_ms` pairs, comma separated. The verdict says `departs` `{class, wait_ms}`; the errand carries `hop.consult_class` and `hop.consult_wait_ms`; its mark stands `pending_ms` (else `consult_pending_ms`).

fallback.description: D58 target: `target:target` pairs, comma separated -- the target a round goes to when the first one gives it up (an unspeakable tool result, a failed answer, too many iterations, `memory_to_brain`). A target with a fallback is a fast one; a verdict without a fallback hands nothing on.

spec_target.description: D58 target: the target of a speculative call (`hop.spec` "1", `quick_speculative`); empty parks every spec curate.

bridge_target.description: D58 target (OR-d58-2.target.14, .38): the target of the side call beside an errand or a tool round (`target` of each entry of the verdict's `side`): one name, or `*:name,spec:name` -- `spec` while the lead speculates, `*` otherwise.

errand_tool.description: D58 target: the name of the tool a speaking model starts an errand with; denied (with `errand_family` when the collector folded it) while an errand of the session stands.

errand_family.description: D58 target: the family of `errand_tool` on the menu, denied with it.

bridge_wording.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476; the curator's knob of D58 target, contract point 14, moved here): the form of the side call beside an errand, per class of `departures`: `<class>:<form>` pairs, comma separated. `soon`: the answer follows in this turn within the class's wait, the side call sees the person's turn alone (`window` `turn`); `later`: the result comes in a later turn, the side call keeps its target's window (`window` `wall`). A class the knob does not name speaks `later`; a form other than these two is dropped.

bridge_texts.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476, contract point 5): the text of a side call per form, a JSON object `{tool, soon, later}` -- `tool` beside the required tool round of a fast target, `soon`/`later` beside an errand by `bridge_wording`. The curator puts it as the leaf of the target's side slot (its profile's `instructions.side_slot`). `{seconds}`/`{minutes}` take the class's wait (`departures`); `{fill}` is the gap the curator fills with the places of the tools the cut left open (`bridge_places`). A form without a text sends no side call. Shipped: the sentences of the curator before the move.

bridge_places.default: {"places": {"weather": "at the weather service", "web": "on the web"}, "rest": "in other places", "before": ", ", "join": " and "}
bridge_places.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476, contract point 1, `fill`): the words of the places a running lookup looks, a JSON object `{places: {family or tool: words}, rest, before, join}`, carried as `fill` on the tool round's side call. The curator names each open tool once (a family with a row by its family name, the hint stage not counted), adds `rest` beside named ones when some have no row, joins them with `join` and puts `before` + the phrase into the gap `{fill}`; nothing named: the gap goes empty. `{}` = no places named.

side_slot.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476, orchestrator ruling moveout.15): the slot the text of a side call stands under (`slot` of each entry of the verdict's `side`) when its target has reported no profile yet; a target's own profile (`instructions.side_slot`) wins. Shipped `bridge`: the leaf `instructions.bridge` of before the move, so the first errand of a colony -- sent beside the target's `catalog_ask` -- keeps its side call. Empty = no `slot`: a target without a profile gets no side call.

horizon_advise.description: GH #1400 (moved from `curator/policy` by D58 moveout, GH #1476): `1` or true = a running session's turn (its question carries the handle `live`) whose first call leaves the composite (an errand class: condition `external`) or gets its required tool round (`must_call`) is told how long the answer takes: ONE entry in the verdict's `feed` -- section `horizon`, a body of numbers only: `seconds` (rounded up), `way`, `family`, never words; the sentence is the voice's `duplex.gpt_live.horizon_text` -- which the curator sends as ONE `live_feed` with the round's sends when the condition holds (held with them for an awaited spec answer, gone when the round never goes), no `hop.at_turn_end`. The seconds are the `horizon_quantile` of the rounds of the turn's family booked so far, else `horizon_defaults_ms[family]`, else nothing is ordered; a turn with several families takes the longest, one without a family counts under its way. Each closed round (the curator's notes `round` and `turn_end` with `round_end`) books its duration (seam to answer, ms) under its family in this lead's store, row `horizon_rounds` (the newest 20 per family), and keeps `horizon_last:<session>` `{turn, family, planned, actual}` (seconds); the mark `feed` of the advise carries `planned` and `family`. `0` (the default) = nothing of this is read, written or ordered.

horizon_defaults_ms.description: GH #1400 (moved from `curator/policy` by D58 moveout, GH #1476): with `horizon_advise` on, the expected duration of a round per family (or way) before any is booked, a JSON object family -> milliseconds (`{"web": 4000}`); a value that is no positive number is said on stderr and left out. `{}` (the default) = no advise until a round of the family is booked.

horizon_quantile.description: GH #1400 (moved from `curator/policy` by D58 moveout, GH #1476): the percentile (nearest rank) of the booked rounds of a family that the advise says, 51 to 100; anything else is said on stderr and read as 75. Never the median: a wait said too short is worse than one said too long.

mark.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476): on `in_feed` -- `{delta_n}`, the words of the partial the interrupt went on; the curator lays it uninterpreted into its mark `feed`

section.description: D58 moveout (GH #1476): on `in_feed` -- `interrupt`, the section of the early interrupt the lead orders

live.description: D58 moveout: on `in_feed` -- the handle of the running session the interrupt goes to ("" without one: the curator books it as not sent)

session_id.description: D58 moveout: on `in_feed` -- the session of the turn

turn_id.description: D58 moveout: on `in_feed` -- the turn the partial belongs to

sender.description: D58 moveout: on `in_feed` -- `lead`, the orderer the curator's mark `feed` names

once.description: D58 moveout: on `in_feed` -- `interrupt`, the key of the curator's claim: one interrupt per turn

description.purpose: The switch of a composite that chooses between targets (GH #1447; the cell `lead` of the hive `lead` since GH #1474). The curator's `./policy` asks once per call (`lead_ask`, beside its ledger reads: the route stamp and the turn's head); the lead reads its own rows in `./state` -- the turn the quick voice gave up, the pending errand, the turn's speculation -- decides `lead_verdict(stamp, head, state)` and answers on `lead_verdict` with `{target, departs, side, feed, reason, spec}`, what the window is built on, and its `handle_ms`; the side calls and the conditional feeds (the waiting-time advise) stand under a condition the curator evaluates. The turn's speculation is its automaton too: the policy hands it each event (`lead_spec`: a spec answer or partial, a stored fallback, a delta stamp, and what a spec call's window showed, `spec_go`, D58 note), the lead moves its rows by compare-and-set and answers with what the move means for the ledger and the sends (`spec_act`); it also decides the early interrupt of a delta stamp. Notes of the policy (`lead_note`: an escalation the wall showed, a consult the model started, a round a condition held for and the turn's end) land in its store; the waiting time of the rounds is booked there. It never reads the ledger and nobody but it reads its store.
